spaces.plausible_today: All small limits of affine k-schemes correspond to colimits of k-algebras. Fiber products use tensor products; equalizers use the quotient by all u(a)−v(a); filtered inverse limits use filtered direct limits of rings. Kernels and stabilizers of affine group actions are the indicated fiber products.

spaces.title: Idempotents and coproduct points
spaces.as_he_states: n’est pas bijective ... k′ connexe — Computation with a questioned punctuation mark; continued next leaf.
spaces.plausible_today: For a finite family of rings A_i, maps ∏A_i→R correspond to orthogonal idempotents e_i summing to 1 and maps A_i→e_iR. The naive disjoint union of point sets is bijective for connected nonzero R, but not general R. The empty affine scheme is strict initial.

spaces.title: Finite relations and geometric quotients
spaces.as_he_states: G/B dans Aff_k est e_k — Warning and example; finite-relation quotient topic deferred.
spaces.plausible_today: Colimits in affine schemes are opposite limits of rings, but can differ from sheaf or scheme quotients. For GL_n and its upper-triangular subgroup, the flag-variety quotient has only constant global functions over a field, so its affine quotient is Spec k.
spaces.state_of_art: C-SA23-spaces-081: The affine versus geometric quotient warning is established (Stacks Groupoids example-quotient-projective-line). Finite locally free equivalence relations are effective: Stacks39.23.9 tag03BM. Mere finiteness does not imply effectivity: Raicu appendix§50 in Kollar2011 pp252–254 gives finite scheme-theoretic relations on A² strictly smaller than the quotient fiber product. Kollar Theorem6 proves geometric quotient existence for finite set-theoretic relations on algebraic spaces essentially of finite type over Noetherian F_p-schemes. Witaszek2022 Theorem1.4 extends existence over excellent bases for separated finite-type algebraic spaces provided the characteristic-zero quotient already exists separated finite type. The manuscript does not specify which notion its “OK” intends. The general characteristic-zero scheme-theoretic existence question is Question8 in Kollar2011; this search did not locate a resolution as of19Nov2026, which is not a certification that it remains open.
